clue.text: What Parisian is in bed with flirty woman?

indicators.note: one piece is said to be lying within the other, as in a bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
the French word for 'what' is que

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a Frenchman says when sharing a bed with a flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What Parisian' asks for the French word, not an English one: a classic crossword way to signal a foreign translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Coquet is an older form for a flirt, a person who trifles with affections, here a woman.

clue.text: Spanish events? Gosh, free! When?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise like gosh
to rid is to free or clear
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly learns of free entry to Spanish festivities and asks the date.
explanation.definitionFit: Corridas are bullfights, the classic public spectacles of Spain; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: A tiny bit of scientific theory

definitions.meaning: a minimal amount or share of something
the physics of discrete energy packets, as in the theory named after them

explanation.surface: Seems to ask for a small fragment of a scientific idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantum is a small fixed amount, and it names the theory of physics built on such amounts.

clue.text: Chemical book hospital disposed of

indicators.note: the hospital letter is got rid of, removed from the book's name

parts.note: Esther is a book of the Old Testament
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A chemical text has been thrown out by a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is a compound formed from an acid and an alcohol, so a kind of chemical.

clue.text: Steward has plan — mice destroyed

indicators.note: the words are wrecked and their letters reassembled into a new order

explanation.surface: A household steward's scheme for dealing with vermin has worked.
explanation.definitionFit: A manciple is the steward who buys provisions for a college or inn, as in Chaucer.

clue.text: One attractive girl can make quite a bit

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a dozen'
pretty means attractive
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A single good-looking girl can earn a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a large sum of money, as in 'that cost me...'.

clue.text: Search shed before a period doing something

parts.note: to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin
a bout is a spell of activity, as in a bout of coughing

explanation.surface: Someone hunts through a garden shed before getting busy for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast about is the idiom for searching around, looking for something.

clue.text: Note about device for fixing shrubs

indicators.note: the note's letters go around the fixing device, enclosing it

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is a note added to a letter
a rivet is a metal pin for fastening plates together

explanation.surface: A memo about a gadget for securing garden shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Privet is a hedging shrub; privets are plants of that kind.

clue.text: Little bird, surprisingly elegant, with any number flying

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an unexpected new order
the number flies off, leaving the word

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A small bird looks surprisingly graceful among a flock in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' takes N out of ELEGANT, leaving ELEGAT, which 'surprisingly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, a small bird yet to grow.

clue.text: One singer by river bridge is famous here

indicators.note: beside, so the river's letter sits next to the rest

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps
I is the Roman numeral one
an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: A lone vocalist performs by a river at a well-known bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto in Venice is the district named for its celebrated bridge over the Grand Canal.

clue.text: Fixing a meeting? Attempt to get smart

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to smart is to sting, as a cut does

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a rendezvous but tries to look smart for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trysting means making a lovers' appointment, an arranged secret rendezvous.

clue.text: Ridiculously big tales when fish is caught? Lots of fish here!

indicators.note: the fish is trapped within the rearranged letters
the letters are scrambled absurdly into a new order

parts.note: a ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Anglers tell absurd tall tales whenever they land a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ridiculously' makes BILSGATE; the first 'fish' is wordplay, the second belongs to the definition. Billingsgate is London's famous fish market.
explanation.definitionFit: Billingsgate is London's wholesale fish market, a place with fish in abundance.

clue.text: Trainee is competent finally to become physician

parts.note: an intern is a trainee, especially a junior doctor

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A trainee is at last competent enough to qualify as a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An internist is a doctor specialising in internal medicine, a type of physician.

clue.text: Woman overwhelmed by mad element

indicators.note: the name is swamped by the surrounding words, buried within them

explanation.surface: A woman is overcome by some crazy force.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a woman's given name, so it fits a definition by example.

clue.text: London building a tram hideously damaged

indicators.note: the words are broken up and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A London tram has been badly wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hideously' looks like an adverb modifying 'damaged', but it is fodder alongside 'a tram'.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiralty House is a historic government building in Whitehall, London, once home to the First Lord of the Admiralty.

clue.text: Soldiers turning up see fellow married at end of book

definitions.text: fellow married at end of book

indicators.note: in a down entry the soldiers' letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
Chester is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Soldiers arrive to witness a man's wedding at a story's close.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'see' is a bishop's diocese, named for its cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Rochester weds the heroine at the close of Charlotte Brontë's novel Jane Eyre.

clue.text: Suspicious-looking chaps? May get someone gossiping aboard ship

indicators.note: the gossip is placed on board, between the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a talker is someone who chatters or gossips

explanation.surface: Shady men may find a chatterbox on board their ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalkers are men who follow people covertly, and may look suspicious in doing so.

clue.text: Club with new temporary accommodation, intended to dispel a feeling of unease

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub
a tent is a shelter used for a short stay

indicators.note: the letter is driven out of the word for intended

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A nightclub with a fresh marquee was meant to ease people's worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontentment is dissatisfaction, a restless, uneasy state of mind.

clue.text: Copper in foreign country, Germany, inclined to fly off the handle

definitions.text: inclined to fly off the handle

indicators.note: the copper symbol sits inside the country's name

parts.note: Iran is a country abroad
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A copper posted abroad and in Germany has a short temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Iracund is a rare word for irritable or quick to anger, given to losing one's temper.

clue.text: Attention given to official herald before the main business?

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention
Lord Lyon is Scotland's chief heraldic officer, the Lord Lyon King of Arms

explanation.surface: An official herald is heard first before proceedings begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Early on means at an initial stage, prior to the main part of events.

clue.text: Fliers if ascending must go over a tree

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are Britain's fliers

indicators.note: in a down entry the little word is read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: Pilots climbing must clear a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is a palm tree of Madagascar, whose leaf fibre is also called by this name.

clue.text: A king beset by fear, tossing and turning?

indicators.note: the king is surrounded by the word for fear

parts.note: awe is reverential fear
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A king lies restless in bed, gripped by dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tossing and turning in bed is not asleep; the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: Leader of revolution is Stalin, violently leaning to the left

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about into a new order
takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Stalin, a revolutionary leader, is said to be leaning violently leftward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of revolution' gives R, mixed with IS STALIN by 'violently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinistral means left-handed or on the left side, from Latin sinister, left.

clue.text: What sounds like swell material

indicators.note: says the entry is pronounced like the word for swell

parts.note: a surge is a swell, as of the sea

explanation.surface: Asks for a fabric whose name echoes something swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen fabric used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: As if aunt would be naughty, giving in to the devil!

indicators.note: the letters misbehave and rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: As though a respectable aunt would misbehave and yield to the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Faustian describes selling one's soul for gain, like Faust's pact with Mephistopheles.

clue.text: See about joining a right good Devon football team

indicators.note: the see's letters are turned round

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Watch a fine right-winger signing for a Devon football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Plymouth Argyle is the professional football club of Plymouth in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyle is the short name of Plymouth Argyle, the Devon city's football club.

clue.text: Story-teller meanders entertainingly — several will drop off

indicators.note: many letters fall away from both ends, leaving a run inside the words

explanation.surface: A rambling narrator goes on so long that several listeners nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: The drop-off here is literal: lose ME from the front and TERTAININGLY from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen was the Danish writer of fairy tales such as The Little Mermaid.

clue.text: Time to get the Olympic-style Jessica into the game

parts.note: Jessica Ennis(-Hill) won Olympic heptathlon gold for Britain in 2012

explanation.surface: Time for an Olympic champion to take up a new sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, one example of a game.
